Palestine Books in Libraries - A UK Micro-Campaign

Why This Campaign?

Justice for Palestine is vital. Recently, Israel has been committing genocide on a people that, inconveniently for Zionists, have been living in this land for centuries. It is far easier for Israel to continue these atrocities when the world does not understand the the occupation.

In their recent genocidal attacks, over 60,000 Palestinians have been killed, with x of these women and y children. Neighbourhoods have been obliterated with use of some of the most advanced military technologies in the world being tested on civilians. People are systematically starved, denied food and medicine. While Israel blames Hamas, this organisation only operates in Gaza, yet violent Isreali attacks in the West Bank are also increasing.

However, this is not a new issue. Since the Nakba of 19xx, Palestinian people have had their lands stolen, their basic human rights denied, and their histories buried. Education is a vital part of resisting Israeli propaganda. In an age of clickbait headlines, fake news and AI generated content, this small campaign aims to provide more accessible, educational and in-depth resources for people in the UK.

The aims of this campaign are modest, but this can be one way among many to resist disinformation and to better understand the Israeli occupation.

Why Libraries?

Put simply, the idea of free books is a radical idea, helping provide local communities with education and enjoyment for no cost. Yet in the UK libraries have been underfunded, with many closing down due to over years of austerity and cuts.

Libraries are easier to close down if people do not use them. By requesting books, you are actively helping keep your local libraries running.

Being part of this campaign means you can help both to keep your libraries open and build an educational resource on Palestine. Through this campaign we hope to:

  • Increase people's knowledge about the Israeli occupation
  • Build and improve local educational resources
  • Reconnect people to their local libraries and communities

Take action!

1. Register

Get a library card at your local public library. It’s usually free and takes 5 minutes.

Find your library on GOV.UK→

2. Check

Search the library catalogue for Palestinian literature – novels, poetry, history, essays. Use the list of suggested titles below to see what you can find and note what is missing.

Suggested books →

3. Ask

Request the library to purchase books they don’t have. Use our template email or speak to a librarian.

Request template →

4. Share

Once your library orders the books, share your request with us on social media so we can share it and update or add a new location!
